options.name: algorithm
options.description: Asymmetric Encryption Algorithm.

options.name: cert_filepath
options.description: path to SSL client cert file (.pem). not supported with python 2.6.

options.name: common_name
options.description: Common name of the certificate. Required for create and install. If name is present, ignored for sign and delete. If name is absent or ignored, required for sign and delete.

options.name: expiry_time
options.description: Certificate expiration time. Specifying an expiration time is recommended when creating a certificate. Can be provided when signing a certificate.

options.name: extended_key_usages
options.description: A list of extended key usage extensions.

options.name: feature_flags
options.description: Enable or disable a new feature. This can be used to enable an experimental feature or disable a new feature that breaks backward compatibility. Supported keys and values are subject to change without notice.  Unknown keys are ignored.

options.name: force_ontap_version
options.description: Override the cluster ONTAP version when using REST. The behavior is undefined if the version does not match the target cluster. This is provided as a work-around when the cluster version cannot be read because of permission issues. See https://github.com/ansible-collections/netapp.ontap/wiki/Known-issues. This should be in the form 9.10 or 9.10.1 with each element being an integer number. When C(use_rest) is set to auto, this may force a switch to ZAPI based on the version and platform capabilit

options.name: generate_csr
options.description: Generate a Certificate Signing Request (CSR) instead of creating or installing a certificate. When true, the CSR is generated based on the provided parameters and returned in the output.

options.name: hash_function
options.description: Hashing function. Can be provided when creating a self-signed certificate, when signing a certificate, or when generating a certificate signing request. Allowed values are sha1, sha224, sha256, sha384, and sha512.

options.name: hostname
options.description: The hostname or IP address of the ONTAP instance.

options.name: http_port
options.description: Override the default port (80 or 443) with this port

options.name: https
options.description: Enable and disable https. Ignored when using REST as only https is supported. Ignored when using SSL certificate authentication as it requires SSL.

options.name: ignore_name_if_not_supported
options.description: ONTAP 9.6 and 9.7 REST API does not support I(name). If set to true, no error is reported if I(name) is present, and I(name) is not used.

options.name: intermediate_certificates
options.description: Chain of intermediate Certificates in PEM format. Only valid when installing a certificate.

options.name: key_filepath
options.description: path to SSL client key file.

options.name: key_size
options.description: Key size of the certificate in bits. Specifying a strong key size is recommended when creating a certificate. Ignored for sign and delete.

options.name: key_usages
options.description: A list of key usage extensions.

options.name: name
options.description: The unique name of the security certificate per SVM. This parameter is not supported for ONTAP 9.6 or 9.7, as the REST API does not support it. If present with ONTAP 9.6 or 9.7, it is ignored by default, see I(ignore_name_if_not_supported). It is strongly recommended to use name for newer releases of ONTAP.

options.name: ontapi
options.description: The ontap api version to use

options.name: password
options.description: Password for the specified user.

options.name: private_key
options.description: Private key certificate in PEM format. Required when installing a CA-signed certificate.  Ignored otherwise.

options.name: public_certificate
options.description: Public key certificate in PEM format. Required when installing a certificate.  Ignored otherwise.

options.name: security_strength
options.description: Security strength of the certificate in bits.

options.name: signing_request
options.description: If present, the certificate identified by name and svm is used to sign the request. A signed certificate is returned.

options.name: state
options.description: Whether the specified security certificate should exist or not.

options.name: subject_alternatives
options.description: Subject alternative names for the certificate.

options.name: subject_name
options.description: Subject name details of the certificate. The format is a list of comma separated key=value pairs.

options.name: svm
options.description: The name of the SVM (vserver). If present, the certificate is installed in the SVM. If absent, the certificate is installed in the cluster.

options.name: type
options.description: Type of certificate Required for create and install. If name is present, ignored for sign and delete. If name is absent or ignored, required for sign and delete.

options.name: use_lambda
options.description: Specifies if AWS Lambda proxy functionality should be used to connect to the ONTAP system. Supported only with REST.

options.name: use_rest
options.description: Whether to use REST or ZAPI. always -- will always use the REST API if the module supports REST. A warning is issued if the module does not support REST. An error is issued if a module option is not supported in REST. never -- will always use ZAPI if the module supports ZAPI.  An error may be issued if a REST option is not supported in ZAPI. auto -- will try to use the REST API if the module supports REST and modules options are supported.  Reverts to ZAPI otherwise.

options.name: username
options.description: This can be a Cluster-scoped or SVM-scoped account, depending on whether a Cluster-level or SVM-level API is required. For more information, please read the documentation U(https://docs.netapp.com/us-en/ontap/authentication/create-svm-user-accounts-task.html). Two authentication methods are supported 1. options.name: validate_certs
options.description: If set to C(no), the SSL certificates will not be validated. This should only set to C(False) used on personally controlled sites using self-signed certificates.
